en: How many times do I have to tell you?
Next time I see you in the forest,
I might shoot, thinking you're a deer,
so please be careful.
Oh, too bad,
it seems you spotted me first.
My hunt has failed,
so now I'm the one who's your prey.
I've set rabbit traps here, too.
Please be careful.
Exactly. You are my prey.
And,
note: no used_in; 'And,' links #330 to #332 (separate message boxes); kept as a bare connective

en: You will be a valuable power to me.
note: capitalised because msg 13413 starts with it; speaker is the protagonist in vampire mode

en: I shall make you a fine servant.
Come to me.
I'm just heading into the forest.
Oh, hey,
I'm about to go hunting.
I'm on my way back from a hunt.
The hunt went well.
My sister Liza lives here with us, too.
I bagged a deer on yesterday's hunt,
note: cut mirrors #303/#304 so the rows read as in the polite version; sentence completed by #342

en: so let me treat you to the venison.
You there, what's your name?
I-I'm
note: must be paired with 'I'm ' in #522 (Aldous, Miltia use #522 + name + #345)
'.' after the name; works for Theodor, Aldous and Miltia (#344 / #522 supply 'I'm ')

en: I see,
note: shared with Queeg: 'I see, Name.' works for both

en: This is a hunting area,
and I can't have people walking in uninvited.
If I shot you by mistake,
there'd be nothing I could do about it.
Eh? Y-yes, I'll be careful.
(I hate to admit it, but I'm intimidated...)
(Compared to when we last met,
note: cut at the same point as the Japanese; 'he' = Theodor (male)

en: he seems quite different...)
Hurry back to the village.
You again? What are you doing?
Do you want to get shot?
If I see you around again,
I might mistake you for a deer and shoot.
So be careful.
Oh, too bad. I missed my shot.
Looks like you spotted me first.
So my hunt is a failure.
Sadly, I seem to have become your prey,
and that's how things stand.
Just so you know, I've set traps, too.
They're for rabbits, but watch your step.
, my master,
I shall do nothing but obey faithfully.
I'm sure I sleep soundly at night,
yet I get the feeling that I've been out
somewhere, now and then...
Good morning.
Oh, we haven't met before, have we?
I am Silas, a shepherd.
I'm just on my way to the pasture.
Oh,
Yes, I'm off to check on my sheep.
Good evening.
I'm just on my way home.
Yes, the sheep are doing well, thank you.
Yes, what can I do for you?
This is Silas, the shepherd.
Yes, we move the sheep elsewhere in winter,
and we go along with them,
so this house stands empty for a while.
Have you met my son, Erwin?
Lately he's been a handful.
Erwin...
note: 'Erwin...' kept neutral so it fits #390 and the other use #425 (slice 005): that row must start with a clause about 'he' ('I wonder if he ...')

en: I wonder if he dislikes being a shepherd.
Oh, forgive me. That has nothing to do with you.
Ah, welcome,
note: variant for Ios (msg 66847), whose line continues without a name

en: Erwin is here, too,
so why don't we chat for a little while?
Won't you try some of our family's stew?
Pleased to meet you.
Is there something I can do for you?
Hello there,
I'm grazing my sheep here.
